notes: 1. SCOPE: This module is the CP Portal Home Dashboard (Customer Registration and Tracking). It is the default landing page after CP login and serves two purposes — (a) tracking all customers the CP has registered (Customers table) and (b) creating new customer/lead registrations. Per visual-memory cp/customer-registration INDEX.md the on-dashboard registration entry point is the 'CREATE NEW LEAD' widget (nationality radio + mobile field + 'Create Lead' button). Sources: BRD/FRD/FS in .claude/docs/hoabl-knowledge-base/CP-Portal + visual-memory/cp/customer-registration/INDEX.md (CAPTURE_STATUS: FULL).

2. AUTH: CP portal is Mobile-OTP only (no password). UAT mobile = 8888888888, CP static OTP = 147258 (per CLAUDE.md — DIFFERENT from the Admin/SM OTP 258369). Login is at the bare /login route; successful login redirects to /dashboard (root '/' when authenticated). Role ID 3 = Channel Partner. An incomplete CP profile (isCpRegistrationCompleted=false) redirects to the RegisterCp profile flow before the dashboard is reachable.

3. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state must be supplied before executing this test. Customer Registration WRITES LIVE customer records on UAT (creates a Registration row, dispatches a real WhatsApp/email to the entered number). Every TC that submits 'Create Lead' / creates a customer MUST be authorised by the user before UAT execution and MUST use only an authorised disposable phone/email. Use 8888888888 only where it is the explicitly authorised fixture; otherwise mark [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED]. No invented PII.

4. MUTATION-AUTHORISATION WARNING: Creating real customer records, triggering duplicate-detection against live data, additional-unit (suffix) registrations, and any submit that fires a buyer notification are DESTRUCTIVE / stateful on UAT. Do NOT execute these without explicit user authorisation (CLAUDE.md Pipeline Discipline Rule 7). Capture-only steps (open the widget, toggle a radio, read the table, type-then-do-not-submit) are safe.
5. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS or not visible in the captured screenshots; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

6. REGISTRATION GLOSSARY: 'Create Lead' = the green full-width button on the CREATE NEW LEAD widget that submits a new customer/lead. 'Register Customer' = the BRD/FRD term for the same registration action (the docs describe a fuller RegisterForm; the live dashboard captures only nationality + mobile — see DOC_DRIFT-003). 'Indian National' / 'NRI' = the two radio options (ant-radio-group name=':r2:'); Indian National is the default. 'HV Code' (e.g. HV00025808) = the CP's unique referral/broker code stored as walkInSourceXrCode on registrations. 'brokerId' = the CP's user ID stamped on every registration they create (drives CP isolation). 'Registration Number' = the unique id of a registration record. 'Allocation Status' = WAITLIST / PREALLOCATED / ALLOCATED / WINNER / HOLD / REFUND. 'Status badge' on the Customers table = Paid (blue pill) / Refunded (red-pink pill).

7. REGISTRATION-NUMBER FORMAT — see DOC_DRIFT-002. The BRD §4.4 / FRD lines 144-153 / FS line 153 say GHNG-XXXXXXXXXX (10 digits, additional units -A/-B/-C). The FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25 (FS line 109, source cp.controller.js) states CP-side registrations actually get an ENCRYPTED SLUG (NOT the GHNG format — GHNG is the buyer-portal format); additional units for the same customer get slug-A, -B, -C. Live implementation wins: TCs assert the registration number is a unique slug and treat the exact human-visible format as [VERIFY WITH DEV] until confirmed against the live Customers table render.

8. NOTIFICATIONS — see DOC_DRIFT-004. On successful CP-side registration the BUYER is notified via WhatsApp template 'cp_link_share_latest' through Botspice (NOT Kaleyra); NRI buyers receive email 'nri-cp-referral'. NO notification is sent to the CP, SM, Admin or Master CP (silent for all CP-side roles — FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25, cp.controller.js). Asserting 'no CP/SM/admin/master-CP notification is dispatched' is a REQUIRED silent-by-design case, not a bug. OTP SMS (login) is delivered via Epinet, not Kaleyra.

9. SECURITY GAP (documented): POST /cp/registration is UNAUTHENTICATED — there is no restrictTo('cp') / auth middleware on the registration route (FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25, cp.routes.js). The endpoint can be hit without a CP JWT. This is a documented gap: do NOT write a '401 without token' PASS case for this endpoint — instead assert the gap and flag it. CP isolation (brokerId / hvCode scoping) is enforced on READ (the Customers table), not on this write route.

10. CP ISOLATION: the Customers table and stats cards show ONLY customers this CP registered (brokerId = CP's user ID); a CP cannot see another CP's customers (BRD §4.1, FRD line 178). KPI/stats counts are CP-scoped. The 'All Team Leads' dropdown scopes the list to a CP's sub-team leads (only relevant for Master/Lead CPs with member CPs under them).

11. KNOWN BUGS (documented in baseline, carried forward): (a) a Master/Lead CP CANNOT create a lead on behalf of a member CP — captured as CP_REG_034 [VERIFY WITH DEV]; (b) when a registration reuses an EXISTING buyer row, the buyer's profile fields are NOT updated from the new form input — captured as CP_REG_032 [VERIFY WITH DEV]; (c) the 'idDraft: true' flag in the registration payload is dead code with no effect — CP_REG_038 [VERIFY WITH DEV]. These are source-derived observations; confirm with dev before treating as authoritative.

12. DOC_DRIFT-001 — CP portal URL: BRD-FS Customer-Registration header (line 4) and BRD §URL say https://uat.xrportal.in/dashboard, and CP-BRD line 6 says '/'. CLAUDE.md (Portals table) and visual-memory INDEX.md (line 5,29) confirm the LIVE authenticated CP dashboard is https://uat-web.xrportal.in/dashboard (or root '/'). Live wins: TC steps use https://uat-web.xrportal.in/. (uat.xrportal.in is the BUYER portal host.)
13. DOC_DRIFT-002 — registration-number format (GHNG vs encrypted slug) — see note 7. CP-side = encrypted slug per cp.controller.js correction; GHNG-XXXXXXXXXX is buyer-portal only.

14. DOC_DRIFT-003 — registration entry point: BRD/FRD/FS describe a full 'Register Customer' RegisterForm (First Name, Last Name, Mobile, Email, Purchase Purpose, Home Loan Intent, Budget, Floor Range, Walk-in Source, T&C checkbox). The captured live dashboard (visual-memory INDEX.md 'Create New Lead Widget') shows only a nationality radio (Indian National / NRI) + a single mobile field + a 'Create Lead' button — the full multi-field form was NOT visible in the dashboard capture. Live capture wins for Step text; the additional RegisterForm fields are tested as [VERIFY WITH DEV] (likely a downstream/second-step form opened after Create Lead, or a separate route not captured). Where a field is asserted that is not in the screenshots, the TC carries [VERIFY WITH DEV].

15. DOC_DRIFT-004 — notification channel (Botspice WhatsApp + NRI email, NOT Kaleyra) — see note 8. FRD §9 / BRD §11 list Kaleyra; the FSD-CORRECTION (cp.controller.js) supersedes this for CP-side registration notifications. Live/source wins.
16. CP OTP = 147258. UAT mobile = 8888888888. Treat the CP portal independently from SM/Admin (CLAUDE.md).

tcs.scenario: To verify the dashboard loads at /dashboard after CP login
tcs.description: Verify that after a successful CP login the browser lands on the Customer Registration dashboard and renders the customer-tracking page.
tcs.precond: A CP account (mobile 8888888888, role 3) with a completed CP profile is available.
tcs.steps:
1. Go to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/login.
2. Enter mobile 8888888888 and submit.
3. Enter OTP 147258 and submit.
4. Wait for the page to finish loading.
tcs.expected: Login succeeds and the browser navigates to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/dashboard (root '/' when authenticated). The Home dashboard renders with the 'Welcome, [cpName]' bar, stats cards, the referral widget, the CREATE NEW LEAD widget and the Customers table. (DOC_DRIFT-001: live host is uat-web.xrportal.in, not uat.xrportal.in.)

1. Enter '123' (or '888888888', 9 digits).
2. Click 'Create Lead'.
tcs.expected: Lead is not created; the widget blocks submission (no API call observed for sub-10-digit values). (Source: visual-memory dashboard-create-lead-invalid-mobile.png — Create Lead with '123' produced no API call / no visible advance.) [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact inline error text, if any.

tcs.scenario: To verify a mobile containing letters is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that a mobile value containing letters fails validation and blocks lead creation.
tcs.precond: Indian National selected.
tcs.steps:
1. Attempt to enter a value with letters in the mobile field.
2. Click 'Create Lead'.
tcs.expected: The mobile is rejected (digits-only field); 'Create Lead' does not submit. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the inline error text.

tcs.scenario: To verify Create Lead with an empty mobile does not submit
tcs.description: Verify that clicking 'Create Lead' with the mobile field empty fires no registration and stays on the dashboard.
tcs.precond: The CREATE NEW LEAD widget is visible with the mobile field empty.
tcs.steps:
1. Leave the mobile field empty.
2. Click 'Create Lead'.
3. Observe the page.
tcs.expected: No registration is created and no API call is fired; the page does not visibly advance (validation blocks submission silently / via a fast-fading inline error). (Source: visual-memory dashboard-create-lead-validation.png.) Per 'silent UX is not a bug' verify no /cp/registration call fired before flagging the missing error. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the inline error styling on the input.

tcs.scenario: To verify Create Lead with invalid mobile '123' is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that an invalid short mobile '123' blocks 'Create Lead' submission.
tcs.precond: Indian National selected; mobile field contains '123'.
tcs.steps:
1. Type '123' in the mobile field.
2. Click 'Create Lead'.
3. Observe the page and network.
tcs.expected: No API call is observed and no lead is created (the button may be disabled below 10 digits). (Source: visual-memory dashboard-create-lead-invalid-mobile.png.) [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm whether the button is disabled vs. shows an inline error.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Budget field accepts numeric values only
tcs.description: Verify that the Budget Amount field rejects non-numeric input.
tcs.precond: The registration form with a Budget field is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the registration form.
2. Try typing letters/symbols in the Budget field.
tcs.expected: The Budget field accepts numeric input only. [VERIFY WITH DEV] DOC_DRIFT-003 — Budget field is not on the captured dashboard widget; confirm decimal/negative handling on the live full form.

tcs.scenario: To verify submitting the empty form shows validation errors
tcs.description: Verify that submitting the registration form with all fields blank surfaces required-field errors and blocks submission.
tcs.precond: The full RegisterForm is open with all fields blank.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the registration form.
2. Without entering anything, click Submit.
tcs.expected: Required-field validation errors are shown on the mandatory fields (First Name, Last Name, Mobile, Email, Purchase Purpose, Home Loan Intent, Budget, T&C) and submission is blocked (FS 2.4). [VERIFY WITH DEV] DOC_DRIFT-003 — the captured dashboard widget validates only the mobile field; confirm the full-form validation behaviour.

tcs.scenario: To verify an invalid email format is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that an email failing standard format validation blocks submission.
tcs.precond: The registration form is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter a malformed email (e.g. 'foo@', 'foo.com', 'foo@@bar').
2. Attempt to submit.
tcs.expected: An email-format validation error is shown and submission is blocked (FS 2.4 Rule 2). [VERIFY WITH DEV] DOC_DRIFT-003 — Email field not on the captured widget; confirm.

tcs.scenario: To verify a missing Purchase Purpose rejects submission
tcs.description: Verify that leaving Purchase Purpose unselected blocks registration (no default value).
tcs.precond: The registration form is open with all fields valid except Purchase Purpose.
tcs.steps:
1. Fill all required fields except Purchase Purpose.
2. Leave Purchase Purpose unselected.
3. Click Submit.
tcs.expected: Submission is rejected with a required-field error on Purchase Purpose (FS 2.4 Rule 5 — required, no default). [VERIFY WITH DEV] DOC_DRIFT-003 — not on the captured widget; confirm.

tcs.scenario: To verify the T&C checkbox must be ticked to submit
tcs.description: Verify that the mandatory Undertaking/T&C consent checkbox must be ticked before the form can be submitted.
tcs.precond: The registration form is filled with all required fields valid but the T&C checkbox unticked.
tcs.steps:

2. Leave the Undertaking/T&C checkbox unticked.
3. Attempt to Submit.
tcs.expected: Submission is blocked (the form cannot be submitted) until the T&C/Undertaking checkbox is ticked (FS 2.4 Rule 4, BRD §4.3 — stored as legal proof). [VERIFY WITH DEV] DOC_DRIFT-003 — checkbox not on the captured widget; confirm.

tcs.scenario: To verify a Floor Range with max < min is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that a Preferred Floor Range whose maximum is below its minimum is rejected.
tcs.precond: The registration form with the Preferred Floor Range fields is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter a minimum floor (e.g. 10).
2. Enter a maximum floor below it (e.g. 5).
3. Attempt to submit.
tcs.expected: A validation error indicates the max floor cannot be less than the min, and submission is blocked. [VERIFY WITH DEV] DOC_DRIFT-003 — Floor Range fields are optional and not on the captured widget; confirm the live cross-field validation.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Cancel button discards entered data
tcs.description: Verify that cancelling the registration form discards any data entered and closes the form without creating a record.
tcs.precond: The registration form is open with some fields filled.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter data in one or more fields.
2. Click Cancel (or close the form).
3. Reopen the form.
tcs.expected: The form closes/resets, no registration is created, and reopening shows empty fields. [VERIFY WITH DEV] DOC_DRIFT-003 — a Cancel control is not visible on the captured dashboard widget; confirm it exists on the full form.

subModules.name: Create New Lead — Submit & System Actions

tcs.scenario: To verify a valid registration submits successfully
tcs.description: Verify that submitting the registration with all required fields valid creates a customer registration.
tcs.precond: A CP is logged in. An authorised disposable customer phone/email is supplied. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable customer mobile + email; user authorisation to create a live record on UAT.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the registration flow.
2. Enter a valid (authorised) mobile and the required details.
3. Tick the T&C checkbox.
4. Click 'Create Lead' / Submit.
5. Wait for the response.
tcs.expected: The registration is accepted, a new Registration record is created (status = Open, paymentStatus = Pending, brokerId = CP's user ID, walkInSourceXrCode = CP's hvCode, availableForAllocation = true) and the customer appears in the Customers table. MUTATION-AUTHORISATION required (note 4).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Create Lead happy path with a valid 10-digit mobile
tcs.description: Verify the end-to-end Create Lead flow: enter a valid Indian mobile, submit, and confirm the new customer is tracked.
tcs.precond: A CP is on /dashboard. An authorised disposable mobile is supplied. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] authorised disposable mobile; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Keep 'Indian National' selected.
2. Type the authorised 10-digit mobile.
3. Click 'Create Lead'.
4. Observe the response and the Customers table.
tcs.expected: The lead is submitted, the registration is created and the new customer row appears in the Customers table; the buyer is notified via Botspice WhatsApp 'cp_link_share_latest' (NRI: email 'nri-cp-referral'). MUTATION-AUTHORISATION required. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the on-screen success feedback (toast/redirect).

tcs.scenario: To verify a submitted registration appears on the Dashboard with status Open
tcs.description: Verify that after a successful registration the new customer row is shown with the initial Open status.
tcs.precond: A registration was just created. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a just-created registration.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a valid registration.
2. Return to / refresh the Customers table.
3. Find the new row.
tcs.expected: The new customer row appears with the initial status reflecting a new registration (record status = Open, paymentStatus = Pending). (FS 2.5.) [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm how 'Open' surfaces in the table's Allocation/Payment Status columns.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Customers table updates after a new registration
tcs.description: Verify that the Customers table reflects a newly created registration in near real-time.
tcs.precond: A CP is on /dashboard. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a just-created registration.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current Customers table rows.
2. Create a new registration.
3. Observe the table.
tcs.expected: The new customer row appears in the Customers table without a manual hard refresh / within a near-real-time update (FS 1.5 Rule 2). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm whether the update is live (websocket/poll) or requires a refresh.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Registration Number format on a created registration
tcs.description: Verify the format of the registration number assigned to a CP-side registration.
tcs.precond: A registration exists for this CP. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an existing registration row.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Customers table.
2. Read the Registration Number column for a CP-side registration.
tcs.expected: The registration carries a unique registration number. DOC_DRIFT-002: per cp.controller.js (FSD-CORRECTION) CP-side registrations get an ENCRYPTED SLUG, not the GHNG-XXXXXXXXXX buyer format; additional units for the same customer get slug-A/-B/-C. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact human-visible registration-number string for CP-side records.

tcs.scenario: To verify an additional unit for the same customer issues a -A suffix
tcs.description: Verify that registering a second unit for an already-registered customer issues a suffixed registration number.
tcs.precond: A customer already has one registration under this CP. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an existing customer with one registration; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Register a second unit for the same customer.
2. Read the new registration number.
tcs.expected: The additional unit registration gets a suffixed number (slug-A, then -B, -C for further units) per FS 2.5.2 / DOC_DRIFT-002. MUTATION-AUTHORISATION required. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the suffix is applied to the encrypted slug (not a GHNG number).

tcs.scenario: To verify an existing buyer row is reused and fields are NOT updated (BUG)
tcs.description: Verify the documented bug that when a registration reuses an existing buyer record, the buyer's profile fields are not updated from the new form input.
tcs.precond: A buyer record already exists for the entered phone/email. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an existing buyer record; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Register a customer whose phone/email matches an existing buyer.
2. Enter different name/details on the form.
3. Submit and inspect the resulting buyer record.
tcs.expected: The existing buyer row is reused and the buyer's profile fields are NOT overwritten with the newly entered values (documented bug, note 11b). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm with dev — this is a source-derived observation.

tcs.scenario: To verify the idDraft flag is dead code
tcs.description: Verify the documented observation that the 'idDraft: true' flag in the registration payload has no functional effect.
tcs.precond: API/source review access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API/source access.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a registration with idDraft true and false (direct API).
2. Compare the resulting records.
tcs.expected: The idDraft flag produces no behavioural difference (dead code, note 11c). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm with dev — source-derived.

tcs.scenario: To verify a duplicate mobile in the same project is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that registering a customer whose mobile already has a registration for this project is rejected.
tcs.precond: A registration already exists for mobile X in this project. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an existing-registration mobile; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the registration flow.
2. Enter the already-registered mobile and required details.
3. Submit.
tcs.expected: Submission is rejected with a duplicate error (the mobile already has a registration for this project) per FS 2.4 Rule 3 / BRD §4.2. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact duplicate-error message text.

tcs.scenario: To verify a duplicate email in the same project is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that registering a customer whose email already has a registration for this project is rejected.
tcs.precond: A registration already exists for email Y in this project. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an existing-registration email; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the registration flow.
2. Enter a new mobile but the already-registered email.
3. Submit.
tcs.expected: Submission is rejected with a duplicate error (the email already has a registration for this project) per FS 2.4 Rule 3. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact message and whether mobile-OR-email both trigger it.

tcs.scenario: To verify the duplicate-mobile rejection from the dashboard widget
tcs.description: Verify the duplicate check fires from the CREATE NEW LEAD widget when the entered mobile already has a registration.
tcs.precond: An existing registration exists for the entered mobile in this project. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] existing-registration mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. On the CREATE NEW LEAD widget enter the already-registered mobile.
2. Click 'Create Lead'.
tcs.expected: The lead is rejected as a duplicate for the project; no new registration is created. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the duplicate message surfaced on the dashboard widget.

tcs.scenario: To verify concurrent capture from two CPs for the same new phone
tcs.description: Verify the race condition where two CPs submit a registration for the same brand-new phone at the same time.
tcs.precond: A brand-new phone not yet registered by anyone; two CP sessions. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] two CP sessions + a new phone; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Prepare two CP sessions (CP-A, CP-B).
2. Submit a registration for the same new phone from both, near-simultaneously.
3. Inspect the resulting records.
tcs.expected: Exactly one registration wins the brokerId/ownership for the new phone; the other is handled as a duplicate (or attaches under the first CP). MUTATION-AUTHORISATION required. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the documented behaviour for the concurrent-capture race.

tcs.scenario: To verify slug-encryption determinism
tcs.description: Verify whether the encrypted registration-number slug is deterministic for the same source id (affects suffix/duplicate behaviour).
tcs.precond: Source/API access to inspect generated slugs. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API/source access.
tcs.steps:
1. Generate registration numbers for known source ids.
2. Compare the encrypted slugs for repeatability.
tcs.expected: The encryption produces a unique slug per registration; determinism for the same source id is confirmed/denied. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the slug-generation determinism (DOC_DRIFT-002, source cp.controller.js).

tcs.scenario: To verify an NRI lead with international-format mobile is accepted
tcs.description: Verify that an NRI customer can be registered using an international country code on the mobile field.
tcs.precond: NRI selected; an authorised disposable international number is supplied. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] authorised disposable NRI number; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Select the 'NRI' radio.
2. Enter an international-format mobile (with country code).
3. Provide the NRI Indian contact number where prompted.
4. Submit.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] authorised NRI international + Indian contact number
tcs.expected: The NRI registration is accepted; the international number is stored and the Indian contact number is captured as nriIndianPhone (FS 2.4 NRI handling). MUTATION-AUTHORISATION required. [VERIFY WITH DEV] DOC_DRIFT-003 — where the country code / nriIndianPhone are captured (not visible on the dashboard widget).

tcs.scenario: To verify effectiveCountryCode drives the NRI WhatsApp dispatch
tcs.description: Verify that the country code used for the NRI buyer notification (effectiveCountryCode) routes the WhatsApp/email correctly.
tcs.precond: An NRI registration was created. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an NRI registration; notification-log access.
tcs.steps:
1. Create an NRI registration with an international country code.
2. Inspect the buyer notification dispatch.
tcs.expected: The effectiveCountryCode value determines the dispatch channel; per FSD-CORRECTION the NRI buyer receives the email 'nri-cp-referral' (and/or Botspice WhatsApp 'cp_link_share_latest' where applicable). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact NRI dispatch routing.

tcs.scenario: To verify the customer receives a Botspice WhatsApp on capture (NOT Kaleyra)
tcs.description: Verify that on successful registration the buyer is notified via the Botspice WhatsApp template, not Kaleyra.
tcs.precond: A registration was created for an authorised number. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] authorised number + notification-log access.
tcs.steps:
1. Create a registration for an authorised disposable number.
2. Inspect the outbound buyer notification.
tcs.expected: The buyer receives WhatsApp template 'cp_link_share_latest' via Botspice (NOT Kaleyra); NRI buyers receive email 'nri-cp-referral' (DOC_DRIFT-004, FSD-CORRECTION). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the dispatch provider in the outbound log.

tcs.scenario: To verify NO notification is sent to CP/SM/Admin/Master CP on registration
tcs.description: Verify the silent-by-design rule that no internal-role notification is dispatched when a CP registers a customer.
tcs.precond: A registration was created. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] notification-log access for CP/SM/Admin/Master-CP channels.
tcs.steps:
1. Create a registration.
2. Inspect outbound notifications to the CP, the CP's SM, Admin and the Master CP.
tcs.expected: No SMS/WhatsApp/email is dispatched to the CP, SM, Admin or Master CP — only the buyer is notified (DOC_DRIFT-004 / note 8). This silence is by design (CLAUDE.md 'silent UX is not a bug'); do not flag the absence of an internal notification as a defect. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm no side-channel internal notification.

tcs.scenario: To verify the dashboard table columns (BRD/FRD set)
tcs.description: Verify that the customer-tracking table exposes the documented BRD/FRD columns.
tcs.precond: A CP with at least one customer is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Read the Customers table header row.
tcs.expected: Per BRD/FRD the table shows Customer Name, Registration Number, Unit Allocated, Allocation Status, KYC Completion and Payment Status. (See TC_CPREG_UI_028 for the live 9-column header captured in visual-memory.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the Customers table heading renders
tcs.description: Verify that the Customers table section heading is shown.
tcs.precond: A CP is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Look at the table section heading.
tcs.expected: A 'Customers' heading is shown above the table. (Source: visual-memory Customers Table.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the live Customers table shows all 9 columns in order
tcs.description: Verify the captured 9-column header of the live Customers table.
tcs.precond: A CP with customers is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Read the table header left to right.
tcs.expected: The header shows, in order: S.No | Applicant Name | Applicant Number | Registration Number | Registration Date | CP Name | CP HV Code | CP Mobile | Status. (Source: visual-memory Customers Table — DOC_DRIFT vs BRD's 6-column list; the live render has 9 columns including CP metadata and Registration Date.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the Allocation Status values shown to the CP
tcs.description: Verify that the allocation status values follow the documented set.
tcs.precond: A CP with customers at varying statuses is on /dashboard. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] customers spanning multiple statuses.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Read the status values shown for the customers.
tcs.expected: Allocation status values are drawn from WAITLIST / PREALLOCATED / ALLOCATED / WINNER / HOLD / REFUND (FRD line 159). The live table additionally shows payment 'Status' badges 'Paid' (blue) and 'Refunded' (red-pink). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm how Allocation Status vs the payment Status badge are presented in the live table.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Unit Allocated cell is blank when not allocated
tcs.description: Verify that a customer with no unit allocated shows a blank Unit Allocated cell.
tcs.precond: A CP has a customer not yet allocated a unit. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an unallocated customer.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Find a customer with no unit.
3. Read the Unit Allocated cell.
tcs.expected: The Unit Allocated cell is blank for customers not yet allocated a unit (FRD line 30). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the live column name (the captured header has no explicit 'Unit Allocated' column — see DOC_DRIFT-003).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Paid status badge renders as a blue pill
tcs.description: Verify that a 'Paid' payment status is shown as a blue pill badge.
tcs.precond: A CP has a customer with Paid status. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a Paid customer.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Find a customer with Paid status.
tcs.expected: The 'Paid' status is shown as a blue pill badge in the Status column. (Source: visual-memory Status badges.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the Refunded status badge renders as a red/pink pill
tcs.description: Verify that a 'Refunded' payment status is shown as a red/pink pill badge.
tcs.precond: A CP has a customer with Refunded status. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a Refunded customer.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Find a customer with Refunded status.
tcs.expected: The 'Refunded' status is shown as a red/pink pill badge in the Status column. (Source: visual-memory Status badges.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the empty-state for a new CP with zero registrations
tcs.description: Verify what the Customers table shows for a CP who has not registered any customers.
tcs.precond: A CP with zero registrations. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP account with no customers.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a zero-customer CP.
2. Land on /dashboard.
3. Look at the Customers table.
tcs.expected: The Customers table renders an empty/no-data state (no rows) and the stats cards show zero counts. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact empty-state placeholder text.

tcs.scenario: To verify Search Customer filters the table by a matching name
tcs.description: Verify that typing a matching name in Search Customer filters the table to matching rows.
tcs.precond: A CP whose customers include 'Sanket' is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Type 'Sanket' in the Search Customer field.
2. Wait ~2.5s for the result to stabilise.
3. Read the table.
tcs.expected: The table filters to rows matching 'Sanket' (the Sanket Test customer in seed data). (Source: visual-memory dashboard-customers-search-result.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify Search Customer shows an empty result for no match
tcs.description: Verify that a non-matching search term yields an empty/no-result table.
tcs.precond: A CP is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Type 'ZZNOTFOUND' in the Search Customer field.
2. Wait for the result.
3. Read the table.
tcs.expected: The table shows the empty/no-result state (no rows; pagination shows 0 items or a 'No data' placeholder). (Source: visual-memory dashboard-customers-search-no-result.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify clearing the search restores the full list
tcs.description: Verify that clearing the Search Customer field restores the unfiltered customer list.
tcs.precond: A search filter is currently applied.
tcs.steps:
1. With a search term applied, clear the Search Customer field.
2. Wait for the table to update.
tcs.expected: The table returns to the full unfiltered list of the CP's customers.

tcs.scenario: To verify the search debounces before updating results
tcs.description: Verify that the Search Customer field debounces (~500-1000ms) before the table updates.
tcs.precond: A CP is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Type a search term character by character.
2. Observe when the table updates.
tcs.expected: The table updates after a short debounce (~500-1000ms) rather than on every keystroke. (Source: visual-memory Search Customer Behaviour — debounce ~500-1000ms.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the All Team Leads dropdown closed-state placeholder
tcs.description: Verify that the team-leads filter shows its placeholder when closed.
tcs.precond: A CP is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Look at the team-leads filter in the table filters row.
tcs.expected: An ant-select with placeholder 'All Team Leads' and a dropdown arrow is shown in the filters row. (Source: visual-memory Customers Table — Filters row.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the All Team Leads dropdown opens and shows 3 options
tcs.description: Verify that opening the team-leads dropdown shows its options.
tcs.precond: A CP (with sub-team leads) is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the 'All Team Leads' dropdown.
2. Read the options.
tcs.expected: The dropdown opens and shows 3 options. (Source: visual-memory dashboard-team-leads-dropdown.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify selecting a team lead filters the table
tcs.description: Verify that selecting a team-lead option scopes the customer list to that team member.
tcs.precond: A Master/Lead CP with member CPs is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:

2. Select a specific team lead.
3. Read the table.
tcs.expected: The table is scoped to the selected team lead's customers (relevant only for CPs with sub-team leads). (Source: visual-memory Team Leads Dropdown.) [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the filter behaviour for a CP without sub-team leads.

tcs.scenario: To verify the page-size selector shows 10/page by default
tcs.description: Verify that the pagination size selector defaults to '10/page'.
tcs.precond: A CP is on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Look at the pagination size selector in the filters row.
tcs.expected: An ant-select shows '10/page' as the default page size. (Source: visual-memory Customers Table — Filters row.)

tcs.scenario: To verify changing the page size affects rows per page
tcs.description: Verify that selecting a larger page size shows more rows per page.

tcs.steps:
1. Open the page-size selector.
2. Choose a larger size (e.g. 50/page).
3. Read the rows-per-page.
tcs.expected: The table renders the chosen number of rows per page (e.g. up to 50). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the available page-size options.

tcs.scenario: To verify navigating to the last partial page
tcs.description: Verify that pagination handles a last partial page of customer rows correctly.
tcs.precond: A CP whose customer count is not an exact multiple of the page size. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP with a non-multiple customer count.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the total customer count and page size.
2. Navigate to the last page.
3. Read the row count and the range label.
tcs.expected: The last page shows only the remaining rows and the range label reflects the partial page (e.g. '21-23 of 23'). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the live pagination range-label format.

tcs.scenario: To verify CP isolation — a CP sees only their own customers
tcs.description: Verify that the Customers table and stats show only customers registered by the logged-in CP.
tcs.precond: Two CPs (CP-A, CP-B) each with their own customers. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] two CP accounts with distinct customers.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as CP-A and note the customers shown.
2. Log in as CP-B and note the customers shown.
tcs.expected: Each CP sees only their own customers (brokerId = that CP's user ID); neither sees the other's customers (BRD §4.1 / FRD line 178).

tcs.scenario: To verify broker isolation on the Customers table (read path)
tcs.description: Verify that the Customers table read path enforces brokerId scoping so only the CP's own customers are returned.
tcs.precond: A CP is logged in on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Land on /dashboard.
2. Inspect the rows returned for the Customers table.
tcs.expected: Only customers with brokerId = the logged-in CP's user ID are returned; no other CP's customers appear (read-path isolation, BRD §4.1).

tcs.scenario: To verify POST /cp/registration is UNAUTHENTICATED (security gap)
tcs.description: Verify the documented security gap that the registration endpoint has no auth/role middleware.
tcs.precond: API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API client; user authorisation (this write creates a live record).
tcs.steps:
1. Call POST /cp/registration with a valid body but NO auth token.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The endpoint accepts the request and creates a registration WITHOUT any auth token — POST /cp/registration is unauthenticated (FSD-CORRECTION, cp.routes.js). Document this as a SECURITY GAP; do NOT write a 401-without-token PASS case (note 9). MUTATION-AUTHORISATION required to actually fire the write. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the gap is still present.

tcs.scenario: To verify capture without the restrictTo('cp') role is rejected (expected vs actual)
tcs.description: Verify the intended role restriction on the capture/registration route versus the documented unauthenticated reality.
tcs.precond: API access with a non-CP token. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a non-CP token; API client.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the capture/registration endpoint with a non-CP (e.g. buyer) token.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: Intended behaviour is rejection for a non-CP role (restrictTo('cp')); however per CP_REG_030 the route is currently unauthenticated, so a non-CP token (or none) is NOT blocked. Document the conflict between intended restrictTo and the unauthenticated route (note 9). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm which is live.

tcs.scenario: To verify a Master CP cannot create a lead on behalf of a member CP (BUG)
tcs.description: Verify the documented bug that a Master/Lead CP cannot create a registration on behalf of a member CP.
tcs.precond: A Master/Lead CP with at least one member CP. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a Master CP + a member CP; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as the Master/Lead CP.
2. Attempt to create a lead scoped to a member CP.
3. Inspect the resulting brokerId.
tcs.expected: The Master CP cannot create a registration on behalf of a member CP — the lead is created under the Master CP's own brokerId (documented bug, note 11a). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm with dev.

tcs.scenario: To verify a tampered/invalid CP session is rejected on the read path
tcs.description: Verify that a tampered or invalid CP JWT fails the protected Customers-table fetch and routes to login.
tcs.precond: A CP is logged in. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] ability to tamper the stored JWT.
tcs.steps:
1. Edit a character of the stored CP JWT.
2. Reload /dashboard.
3. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: The protected Customers-table API call fails (401) and the CP is redirected to /login. (Note: this is the READ path; the WRITE registration route is unauthenticated per CP_REG_030.) [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the read-path 401 redirect.

tcs.scenario: To verify the projectId is set by environment, not user input
tcs.description: Verify that the registration's project is determined by environment configuration (hardcoded by NODE_ENV), not chosen by the CP.
tcs.precond: API/source access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API/source access.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a registration on UAT.
2. Inspect the projectId stamped on the record.
tcs.expected: The projectId is fixed by the environment (NODE_ENV-based hardcode; Strapi project id=1 is fetched directly by the CP frontend per FRD §9 correction) — the CP does not select a project. The duplicate check is therefore scoped to this single project. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the UAT projectId value.

tcs.scenario: To verify a successful registration syncs the customer downstream
tcs.description: Verify that a successful CP-side registration creates the downstream customer/lead record used by other modules.
tcs.precond: A registration was created. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] downstream record visibility; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Create a registration.
2. Inspect the downstream customer/registration record and any LSQ lead sync.
tcs.expected: A Registration record exists with brokerId = CP's user ID and walkInSourceXrCode = CP's hvCode; the new customer becomes visible in the CP's Customers table and is available for allocation (availableForAllocation = true). LSQ is EXCLUDED from QA scope (CLAUDE.md) — do not assert LSQ side-effects. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the downstream record shape.

tcs.scenario: To verify the registration API accepts a valid body (API)
tcs.description: Verify that POST /cp/registration with a valid body returns success and creates a registration.
tcs.precond: An API client is available; an authorised disposable customer payload. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API client + authorised payload; user authorisation (live write).
tcs.steps:
1. POST /cp/registration with valid customer fields, hvCode and projectId.
2. Read the HTTP status and body.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns success and creates a Registration (status Open, paymentStatus Pending, brokerId, walkInSourceXrCode, availableForAllocation true). Base URL https://uat-api.xrportal.in/. MUTATION-AUTHORISATION required. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact request/response contract.

tcs.scenario: To verify the registration API rejects a duplicate at the backend (API)
tcs.description: Verify that the backend duplicate check rejects a registration whose mobile/email already exists for the project.
tcs.precond: An API client; an existing-registration mobile/email. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API client + existing-registration data.
tcs.steps:
1. POST /cp/registration with a mobile/email that already has a registration in this project.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The backend rejects the duplicate (mobile OR email already registered for this project) per FS 2.4 Rule 3. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the error status/body.

tcs.scenario: To verify the registration API is more permissive than the UI (validation split)
tcs.description: Verify whether the backend enforces the same field validations as the UI form (UI-vs-backend split).
tcs.precond: An API client. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API client.
tcs.steps:
1. POST /cp/registration omitting a UI-required field (e.g. T&C/Undertaking flag, Purchase Purpose) or with a malformed email.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the UI mandates T&C/Purchase Purpose/email format; confirm whether the unauthenticated backend route enforces the same validations or accepts a partial/malformed body (validation bypass). Given the route is unauthenticated (CP_REG_030), backend permissiveness is plausible — document any bypass found.

tcs.scenario: To verify injection at the registration API is safely handled
tcs.description: Verify that SQLi/XSS payloads sent to the registration API are not executed and do not leak DB errors.
tcs.precond: An API client. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API client.
tcs.steps:
1. POST /cp/registration with injection payloads in the name/email/mobile fields.
2. Read the response and check for DB error / script reflection.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the backend should use parameterised queries and reject/escape the payload with no SQL error and no script reflection. Confirm backend sanitisation (the route is unauthenticated, so this is a higher-risk surface — CP_REG_030).

tcs.scenario: To verify a server 500 on Create Lead surfaces a user-facing error
tcs.description: Verify that a backend failure on submit shows a friendly error and lets the CP retry without losing the form.
tcs.precond: The registration form is filled; a 500 can be simulated on the registration endpoint.
tcs.steps:
1. Fill a valid registration.
2. Force the registration endpoint to return 500 (DevTools).
3. Click 'Create Lead' / Submit.
tcs.expected: A user-friendly error is shown, any spinner clears and the CP can retry; no partial record is left in an inconsistent state. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact error message and that no duplicate record is created on retry.

tcs.scenario: To verify a network failure on Create Lead is handled gracefully
tcs.description: Verify that a dropped network on submit does not silently lose the registration or create a duplicate.
tcs.precond: The registration form is filled; the network can be cut.
tcs.steps:
1. Fill a valid registration.
2. Go offline / block the request.
3. Click 'Create Lead'.
4. Restore the network and retry.
tcs.expected: An error/retry affordance is shown; on retry exactly one registration is created (no duplicate from the failed first attempt). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the offline handling and idempotency on retry.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Customers table handles a fetch failure gracefully
tcs.description: Verify that a failed Customers-table fetch shows an error/empty state rather than a blank crash.
tcs.precond: A CP is on /dashboard; the customers fetch can be forced to fail.
tcs.steps:
1. Force the Customers-table fetch to return an error (DevTools).
2. Reload /dashboard.
3. Observe the table region.
tcs.expected: The table region shows an error/empty state (not a blank or broken page) and the rest of the dashboard remains usable. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact error/empty placeholder.
